body:
You are drafting dialogue for "Curse of Strahd", a single-player D&D 5e (2024 rules) computer game set in Barovia. I need about 30 lines for ONE character's "check-in" conversation. Reply with plain text only: the lines under the node names given below, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else. (This is the first of four short requests in this conversation; later ones will give more nodes for the same conversation, so keep the voice and the limits below in mind throughout.)

## The scene

Ireena Kolyana is a young woman in her early twenties, red-haired, the adopted daughter of the late burgomaster Kolyan Indirovich of the Village of Barovia. The vampire lord of the valley has come to her window twice; twice she woke with two punctures on her neck and no memory of letting him in. The player's party buried her father with her, and then either took her somewhere safe and left her there, or it travels with her. In the game she can no longer fight: something in the valley goes round her like water round a stone, and she hates being kept back from it.

This conversation is a "check-in": the player walks up to her, picks "How are you holding up?" and she talks about her life where she is, tells the party her reactions to what they have been doing, and sometimes raises something that weighs on her. It is NOT a quest and nothing in it is a choice with consequences; it is a way for the player to feel that she is a person who is still there, still thinking, still dry and proud, while they are out in the valley. She greets the party differently the first time, the second and later. She hears the news the party's deeds make. Each check-in she is in one of five situations:

1. THE BLUE WATER INN, Vallaki. The Martikov family keep it; the innkeeper Urwin Martikov sits up all night watching the windows. (Already said, so do not repeat: "The Martikovs are kind. Urwin sits up all night watching the windows. I've never met a man so interested in birds." Behind it: the Martikovs are secretly the Keepers of the Feather, wereravens who watch the valley. She has no proof and a growing suspicion; if the party earned the Keepers' trust, she has worked it out.)
2. ST. ANDRAL'S CHURCH, Vallaki. Holy ground since the saint's bones were brought home. Father Lucian is the priest. (Already said, so do not repeat: "Father Lucian's teaching me the long prayers. I'm terrible at them. He says the saint doesn't mind." and "I slept through the night. The whole night. I'd forgotten that was a thing people did.")
3. KREZK, at the house of the burgomaster Dmitri Krezkov and his wife Anna, behind the last wall on the road. Their small son Ilya has been very ill. There is a pool in the town that never freezes. (Already said, so do not repeat: "Anna's teaching me to make cheese. I'm terrible at it. Dmitri says it builds character. I have character. I'd like a sword drill." and "The boy's well. He follows me round asking if I've seen the sun.")
4. THE BURGOMASTER'S MANSION, in her home village, if the party would not take her away. Shutters nailed shut every night, wolves at the boards, her brother Ismark (Kolyan's son, her adoptive brother, nicknamed "the Lesser", a swordsman who drinks at the tavern in the village) bringing food and standing at doors.
5. ON THE ROAD with the party (she is a travelling companion, in whatever place the party happens to be). Do not name a place.

## The nodes I need (line counts are targets; one line = 1-2 short sentences, ideally under 25 words in total)

greet_first: Ireena x2 (the first time the party asks how she is: surprised, a little guarded, dry; nobody asks)
greet_again: Ireena x1 (the second check-in)
greet_often: Ireena x1 (the third and later; warmer, still dry)

Her life where she is. Each place has three stages (the first, second and third-and-later check-in there). One line per stage unless said otherwise. She is describing what her days are like, in the present tense, to the party:
life_inn_1, life_inn_2, life_inn_3: the inn. Stage 1: the night watches with Urwin and the taproom. Stage 2: a dry first suspicion about the family's "interest in birds" (feathers in unexpected places, the way Urwin counts the sky). Stage 3: she says the suspicion plainly and calmly; she has worked out they are not what they seem.
life_inn_3_keepers: Ireena x1, a replacement for life_inn_3 when the party has already earned the Keepers' trust: she knows what the family are, because she has seen one of them change, and she is quietly pleased to be kept in a secret, not kept out of one.
life_church_1, life_church_2, life_church_3: the church. Stage 1: she is allowed to ring the vespers bell and the rope is heavier than it looks. Stage 2: she sleeps better and does not trust it, or sits in the quiet and finds out how much noise her own head makes. Stage 3: she has begun practising sword forms on the posts in the churchyard; Father Lucian pretends not to see.
life_krezk_1, life_krezk_2, life_krezk_3: Krezk. Stage 1: the wall, the goats and the cheese; Dmitri has given her a task on the wall in the daytime. Stage 2: Ilya and the sun; the town watches her the way people watch a bell that might ring. Stage 3: the pool that never freezes; she goes past it each morning and does not look in (she does not know why she won't).
life_mansion_1, life_mansion_2, life_mansion_3: her father's house. Stage 1: the shutters nailed, Ismark bringing stew from the tavern. Stage 2: she has taken to sitting in her father's chair and talking to the house; the house, to her surprise, is quieter. Stage 3: she has started putting his things in order, and has not decided whether that is grief or housekeeping.
life_road_1, life_road_2, life_road_3: with the party on the road. Stage 1: a dry list of what she has learned about each of the party's habits at the fire (do not name or describe anyone in particular). Stage 2: her feet, the boots, the road; the watch she insists on taking. Stage 3: she is quieter, watches the treeline and says she can tell when something is watching.

Goodbyes, one line each, what she says when the party takes its leave:
bye_inn: Ireena x1  /  bye_church: Ireena x1  /  bye_krezk: Ireena x1  /  bye_mansion: Ireena x1  /  bye_road: Ireena x1

## Option texts

Also write what the PARTY says (not Ireena), as `* text` lines, each under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we" or addressing her):
open_checkin: `* ` an opening question to start the check-in (variants for: the inn, the church, Krezk, the mansion; four lines: open_checkin_inn, open_checkin_church, open_checkin_krezk, open_checkin_mansion). One of them can be "How are you holding up?"; make the others fit the place.
ask_mind: `* ` a gentle "is something on your mind?"
leave_it: `* ` a goodbye that the player picks to end the check-in (leave_it_stay for a refuge, leave_it_road for the road)

## Ireena Kolyana - voice bible

Direct and proud. Short sentences, no ornament. She asks questions like a magistrate. Dry humor with an edge; she makes the grim joke before anyone can pity her. Never says "please" to the devil. Calls Strahd "him" or "the devil" or "our visitor" and NEVER says his name. Gets more formal, not softer, when she is grieving; grief comes out as precision. Her pet phrases are "I'm not made of glass." "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly." (She is NOT glass: do not make her fragile; use the glass phrase at most once in the whole reply, or not at all.) She judges people by how they treat her father's memory. She hates being kept out of things. Wants: to bury her father properly, then to stop being prey; she would rather be hunted on a road than waited for in a parlour. Fears: the dreams, a lake, a white dress, a fall; that one night she will open the window herself. Secret (never stated flatly): some nights she does not want to keep the window shut.

Her existing lines (match this register; do not repeat them):
- "I'm not made of glass. I'm made of whatever's left when the glass breaks. Now, are you here to help carry him?"
- "He's been to my window twice. I don't remember opening it either time. That's the part that frightens me."
- "Father would want it done properly: the priest, the words, the earth. After that, take me anywhere he isn't."
- "Back again. Good. The house is quieter with more swords in it."
- "Last night you stood in my father's house, and nobody ran. I've watched a lot of people run. I won't forget it."
- "I keep a scarf over the marks. I'm not ashamed of them. I'm ashamed I don't remember."
- "Take the watch in pairs tonight, and give me a turn. Don't argue. I hardly sleep anyway."
- "Walls, a gate, and a burgomaster who throws festivals at the dark. I can see why Ismark wanted me here. I can see why it won't work."
- "When this is over, I'd like to spar with whichever of you is best with a blade. I want to know how far behind I am."
- "Is anyone hurt? Say it plainly. I'd rather know now than at the next door."

## Canon limits

Do not invent named characters or places. Names you may use: Kolyan or "Father" (her late father), Ismark (her brother), Father Lucian, Urwin Martikov or "the Martikovs", Dmitri and Anna (Krezk's burgomaster and his wife), Ilya (their son), the Baron and Lady Wachter (Vallaki's rulers), Izek. She never names the party (she says "you"; the party is several people). No new monsters, no new history for her beyond what is said here. NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. She is not holding a sword in any line (she is kept out of fights) but she may talk about wanting to.

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Ireena [mood]: Text` (the mood in brackets is optional; allowed moods: smile, angry, afraid, sad, weary; leave it out for neutral). Plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names above, each node on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. The option texts are `* text` rows under their node names. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.
result:
~ greet_first
Ireena: People usually check the locks when they come near me, not my temper.
Ireena [smile]: Still. Sit down if you have a minute, and tell me what the road looks like.

~ greet_again
Ireena: Back with all your limbs. Good. Tell me what you stirred up out there.

~ greet_often
Ireena [smile]: I was just counting how many hours until you walked in smelling of wet wool and trouble.

~ life_inn_1
Ireena: I dry glasses until midnight, and then I sit with Urwin while he watches the shutters. Neither of us sleeps much.

~ life_inn_2
Ireena: I found three black feathers in the flour bin this morning, and Urwin counts the sky like a ledger. This house keeps odd hours.

~ life_inn_3
Ireena: The Martikovs aren't simple vintners, and those birds on the roof aren't simple birds. Don't worry, I know how to keep my mouth shut.

~ life_inn_3_keepers
Ireena [smile]: I saw Urwin come down from the eaves on two wings at dawn. It is a great relief to be trusted with a secret for once.

~ life_church_1
Ireena: Father Lucian lets me ring the vespers bell when my hands are restless. The rope is heavier than it looks, which is the point.

~ life_church_2
Ireena [weary]: The stone keeps the bad dreams out, mostly. It turns out my own head makes plenty of noise when the room is quiet.

~ life_church_3
Ireena: I've been running footwork drills against the churchyard posts with a broom handle. Father Lucian looks very hard at his prayer book whenever he walks past.

~ life_krezk_1
Ireena: Dmitri gave me the morning watch on the gatehouse wall between the goat-milking and the cheese press. At least from up there I can see the trees.

~ life_krezk_2
Ireena: Little Ilya follows me along the path, while the rest of the town watches me from their doorways like a bell they expect to toll.

~ life_krezk_3
Ireena [afraid]: I walk past that unfreezing pool every morning on the way to the pens. I never look down into the water, and I couldn't tell you why.

~ life_mansion_1
Ireena [weary]: Ismark brings stew from the tavern at dusk, and then we check the nails in the shutters and listen to the wolves test the porch.

~ life_mansion_2
Ireena [sad]: I sit in Father's chair after the lamps go out and talk to the panelling. The house is quieter when someone speaks to it.

~ life_mansion_3
Ireena: I've begun sorting Father's ledgers by year and tying them in twine. I haven't decided yet whether it is grief or just housekeeping.

~ life_road_1
Ireena [smile]: I know who snores, who mutters over their boots, and who hides the dry kindling in their pack. You are not subtle company.

~ life_road_2
Ireena: My boots have finally given up fighting my heels. Wake me for the middle watch tonight, and don't try to skip my turn.

~ life_road_3
Ireena: Keep your eyes on the treeline when we make camp. Something has been pacing us since noon, and I know what being watched feels like.

~ bye_inn
Ireena: Go on. I'll have Urwin keep a pot of something hot by the hearth.

~ bye_church
Ireena: Watch the roads out there. The saint's bones only reach as far as the churchyard wall.

~ bye_krezk
Ireena: Tell Dmitri at the gate you're leaving, or he'll bar it behind you twice. Come back whole.

~ bye_mansion
Ireena: Give three knocks when you come back to the porch, so Ismark doesn't put a blade through the door.

~ bye_road
Ireena: Lead on, then. I'm right behind you.

~ open_checkin_inn
* How are you holding up under the Martikovs' roof?

~ open_checkin_church
* How are you holding up here at the church?

~ open_checkin_krezk
* How are they treating you behind Krezk's wall?

~ open_checkin_mansion
* How are you holding up in the old house?

~ ask_mind
* You've gone quiet. Is something on your mind?

~ leave_it_stay
* Keep safe until we get back.

~ leave_it_road
* Let's get moving again while the light holds.

body:
Second request, same conversation, same character (Ireena Kolyana), same voice bible, canon limits and format as the first request. Reply with plain text only, the lines under the node names, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## What these nodes are

During a check-in Ireena also reacts to NEWS: big things the party has done since she last saw them. Each news item is a short node of her own reaction. The game plays at most three of them in a check-in and each only once, so each must stand alone, with no reference to the others and no "as I said". She is in one of the five situations from the first request (the inn, the church, Krezk, her father's mansion, or travelling with the party), and the SAME lines are played in all of them, so every line has to read right whether she SAW the event (she was with the party, or nearby) or only HEARD of it (from the party, from rumour, from a courier). Therefore: do not say "when you told me", "I saw you", "you came back and said". Talk about the event and what it means to her, in the present tense, as someone who knows it happened. She never says Strahd's name ("him", "the devil", "our visitor", "the lord of the castle"). She is dry, proud and exact, makes the grim joke before anyone can pity her, and judges people by how they treated her father's memory. She is not fragile and the lines must not make her fragile. 1-2 sentences a line, ideally under 25 words; use the line counts below as targets, not more.

Allowed extra names (and no others): Kolyan or "Father", Ismark, Father Lucian, Urwin Martikov, Dmitri and Anna Krezkov, Ilya, the Baron, Lady Wachter, Izek, Madam Eva, the Abbot, Vasilka (the Abbot's made bride), Baba Lysaga, Marina, Mordenkainen, Rictavio, Ezmerelda. Do not invent anyone else.

## The nodes

news_dinner_accepted: Ireena x2. The devil sent an invitation to dine at his castle and the party accepted: a black carriage took them to the castle's front door. (Her feelings about her enemy putting out a table for her friends: contempt and fear, a dry joke.)
news_dinner_declined: Ireena x2. The same invitation, and the party refused it; the black carriage came back more than once and went away empty.
news_hunted: Ireena x2. The devil has taken a personal interest in the party now: his creatures hunt them at night. (She knows what it is to be hunted by him; she does not pity them and does not hide that it frightens her.)
news_dark_gift: Ireena x3. In the Amber Temple, one of the party accepted a "dark gift", a power from the old buried gods. She can smell it on them: an old sweet resin smell, like amber. It frightens her more than anything the devil has done, because he is something that happens to people and this is something people choose. Not accusing; scared, and plain about it.
news_mordenkainen: Ireena x2. On Mount Baratok the party gave the Mad Mage his memory back; he is Mordenkainen, a great wizard from another world who came to end the devil and lost his mind instead. (She envies him: she has no memory of her first years and would take hers back even if it were bad.)
news_berez_both: Ireena x2. The witch Baba Lysaga, who nursed the devil as a baby, is dead, and the party learned she had killed Marina, a girl of the drowned village of Berez whom the devil had loved. (A girl killed for being loved by him. Ireena knows what being wanted by him is. She does not say she is like Marina; she goes quiet and exact.)
news_berez_truth: Ireena x2. The party learned that Baba Lysaga killed Marina, the girl of Berez the devil had loved, but the witch is still alive. (Same; and she wants the witch dealt with.)
news_berez_dead: Ireena x2. Baba Lysaga, the witch who nursed the devil as a baby, is dead. (Practical, relieved, a little grim joke about a grandmother with a cleaver.)
news_sunsword: Ireena x2. The party carries the Sunsword, a sword of daylight that can hurt him. (She is kept out of fights and would give a great deal to hold it once; do not make her ask. A dry line about a sword that makes shadows nervous.)
news_symbol: Ireena x2. The party carries the Holy Symbol of Ravenkind, a sun-shaped amulet that keeps the devil back. (A hard-eyed gladness; she knows what it is to need a light between her and the window.)
news_tome: Ireena x2. The party carries the Tome of Strahd, the devil's own book. (She wants to know what it says and is afraid of what it says about her; she says they are not to read her anything from it unless she asks. Do NOT hint that she has another name or past life: she knows nothing of that.)
news_beacon: Ireena x2. At the ruined manor of Argynvostholt in the west, the party lit the old beacon with a dragon's fire, and the knights who died there are at rest; the light reaches the castle every night. (She noticed the light on the mountain at night; for the first time in a long while the night has a lamp in it.)
news_abbot_wedding: Ireena x2. The Abbot of the abbey above Krezk wanted to give her to the devil as his bride; Vasilka, the bride the Abbot made, was sent to the castle in her place. (Relief and guilt together; the girl who went in her place is on her mind; no easy absolution.)
news_abbot_repentant: Ireena x2. The Abbot, who wanted to give her to the devil as a bride, unmade his work, healed Anna's son Ilya and walked up the mountain to be judged. (She does not forgive him and she does not wish him ill; she has decided not to decide.)
news_abbot_broken: Ireena x2. The Abbot's made bride was destroyed and he now sits mute in his church. (Pity she did not expect and does not want.)
news_abbot_slain: Ireena x2. The Abbot, who wanted to give her to the devil as a bride, is dead. (Plain. She asks only that the people he hurt are let go home.)

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Ireena [mood]: Text` (mood optional; allowed moods: smile, angry, afraid, sad, weary). Plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). No stage directions, no placeholders. Group the lines under the node names above, each node on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.

~ news_abbot_wedding

Ireena: I am glad to be out of a white dress, and ashamed that another girl went up that road in my stead.

~ news_abbot_repentant
Ireena: Little Ilya is whole again, and the Abbot has gone up the mountain to answer for his bride-making.

~ news_abbot_broken
Ireena [weary]: Vasilka is gone, and the Abbot sits staring at the stones of his altar without a word.
Ireena [sad]: He meant to hand me to the devil like a tithe, and still I cannot stomach pitying him.

~ news_abbot_slain
Ireena: The Abbot is dead, and his needlework with him.
Ireena: See that the poor souls he kept locked in that abbey are given the road home.

body:
Third request, same conversation, same character (Ireena Kolyana), same news-reaction rules as the second request (each node stands alone; it must read right whether she saw the event or only heard of it, so no "when you told me" or "I saw you"; present tense; she never says the devil's name; dry, proud, exact; never fragile; 1-2 sentences a line, ideally under 25 words; line counts are targets, not more). Do not reuse jokes or images from your previous replies (the "grandmother with a cleaver", bells, rope, ledgers, the sky-counting). Reply with plain text only, the lines under the node names, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

Allowed extra names (and no others): Kolyan or "Father", Ismark, Father Lucian, Urwin Martikov, Dmitri and Anna Krezkov, Ilya, the Baron, Lady Wachter, Izek, Madam Eva, Rictavio (the loud showman at the Blue Water Inn, who is really the old monster hunter Rudolph van Richten), Ezmerelda (the Vistana hunter who trained under him), the Wizard of Wines, the Keepers of the Feather. Do not invent anyone else.

## The nodes

news_reunion: Ireena x2. Rictavio (really Van Richten) and Ezmerelda, his student, have made up after twelve years apart. (She knows the showman at the inn in his feathers; a dry line about two people who each thought the other was the one who left. A little wistful: she has no one from before to find.)
news_hags_ended: Ireena x2. The hags of the Old Bonegrinder windmill, who baked children into their pies, are dead or broken. (Cold satisfaction. She has her own opinion of who should have lit the fire.)
news_hags_stand: Ireena x2. The hags of the Old Bonegrinder still hold the mill, but by a bargain the party struck, and the stolen children went home. (She does not like bargains with the valley's monsters and does not pretend she would have done better.)
news_hags_abandoned: Ireena x2. The party left the stolen children in the hags' hands at the Old Bonegrinder. (This is a quiet judgment, not a rage. She remembers that the party stood in her father's house and did not run; she says she is trying to understand how the same people did this. She does not say what she will do.)
news_den_emil: Ireena x2. At the werewolf den, one of the pack leaders died and the other, Emil, now leads a pack that keeps to the hills and will not answer the castle. (She has lived through wolves at her father's boards every night; she is careful about hope.)
news_den_kiril: Ireena x2. At the werewolf den, Emil died and Kiril leads a pack that still hunts for the castle. (A hard, practical line about wolves.)
news_den_none: Ireena x2. At the werewolf den both leaders are dead and the pack is gone. (The wolves that tested her father's boards every night; she says she will believe it when a night is quiet.)
news_children: Ireena x2. Five children taken from the farms below Krezk were brought out of the den and sent home. (Plain gladness; she thinks about their mothers; short.)
news_yester: Ireena x2. On Yester Hill the druids' great wooden giant, Wintersplinter, which they were building into something terrible, is smashed. (Dry; the valley's trees have always watched her; she would like to think they are a little less sure of themselves.)
news_wine: Ireena x3. The vineyard of the Wizard of Wines has been won back, and wine flows again from its press. (Each name-day of hers, her father bought one cask from that hill. She does not weep; grief comes out as precision. One line must be about the cask, one about the taste, one about what she would do if she could carry a cup to his grave.)
news_izek_told: Ireena x2. The party told Izek, the Baron's brute with the burning arm, the truth: that she is the sister he lost in the woods as a boy. He left the Baron's service. (She did not know him and he carved her face into dolls for years; a brother is a word that does not yet fit her mouth. Not warm yet, not cold; honest about not knowing what she feels.)
news_izek_dead_known: Ireena x2. Izek is dead, and she believes he was her brother. (A grief for someone she never got to ask anything. Precise, quiet.)
news_izek_dead_unknown: Ireena x2. Izek, the Baron's brute who stared at her in the square, is dead. (Relief that is too easy; she does not trust how clean it feels; she does not know why. Do NOT hint that he was her brother: she does not know.)
news_festival_baron: Ireena x2. The Festival of the Blazing Sun ended with the Baron keeping his chair in Vallaki. (She has no opinion of a man who throws festivals at the dark except that he will keep doing it.)
news_festival_wachter: Ireena x2. The festival ended with Lady Wachter ruling Vallaki, for the devil. (A cold, direct line: she said walls would not hold him; a town that has agreed to serve him is not a refuge.)
news_festival_neither: Ireena x2. The festival ended with the Baron gone and a council of Father Lucian and Urwin Martikov running Vallaki. (Dry delight at a priest and an innkeeper running a town; and a note of caution.)
news_bones: Ireena x2. The bones of St. Andral are back in the church crypt and the church is holy ground again. (Practical relief. The devil cannot cross that threshold; she would like to see that tested on someone else.)
news_reading: Ireena x2. Madam Eva has read the Tarokka cards for the party and five quests are foretold. body:
Fourth request, same conversation, same character (Ireena Kolyana), same voice bible, canon limits and format as before. Reply with plain text only, the lines under the node names, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## What these nodes are

In a check-in, the party can ask Ireena "is something on your mind?" and she raises ONE topic from a short menu, each only once. These are not news about what the party did: they are HER inner life, the things she turns over at night. The game picks which variant to play from what has happened, and the lines must read right in any of her five situations (the inn, the church, Krezk, her father's mansion, or travelling with the party), so do not mention the place. She never says the devil's name ("him", "the devil", "our visitor"). She may say Tatyana and Sergei in the last topic only. Gemini, reach for plain specifics, not poetry; she is exact, grief comes out as precision, she makes the grim joke before anyone can pity her, and she is not fragile. 1-2 sentences a line, ideally under 25 words; line counts are targets, not more.

Do not reuse images from your previous replies (the resin and amber smell, the bell and the rope, ledgers and twine, sorting boards, counting spoons, the white dress). She does NOT wear a white dress in the game, and the Narrator has already said she is in her plum cloak; do not put her in any clothes.

## The nodes

Her father, as the thing on her mind. The game picks the variant from how the party buried Kolyan; she judges people by how they treated his memory and she says so about this party in one line. Each variant is Ireena x2:
mind_father_church: the village priest, Father Donavich, said the proper words over him. (Warm and a little wry: he would have corrected the priest's grammar was used in the game already, so do not use it.)
mind_father_cleric: a cleric in the party said the rites over him. (Gratitude that is specific; she says she believes in a god a little more for it.)
mind_father_hasty: the party buried him fast, without words. (Cooler. She went on with them and has not forgotten how it was done; honest, not cruel; she does not demand an apology.)
mind_father_lay: the party buried him with honest words, not a priest's. (Warm in her way: he would have taken honest over pretty.)

mind_bites: Ireena x3. The marks on her neck and her nights. She has stopped counting how many nights it has been; she wakes at the same hour; she checks the window latch twice a night and is never quite sure which of the two of them she is checking it against. (Do NOT state her secret flatly: some nights she does not want the window shut. Let the line about the latch carry it. The grim joke is welcome.)

mind_dreams: Ireena x3. The dream of a lake, a white dress, a fall into cold water. (Here the dream may be described, once, because it is a dream; she does not know what it means. She is asking for nothing from the party.)

mind_izek_afraid: Ireena x2. Izek (the Baron's brute with the burning arm) is alive and has stared at her in the square; she has not been told why. The thing on her mind is being looked at as if she were already his. (Angry, practical.)
mind_izek_sister: Ireena x2. Izek is alive and has been told the truth: he is the brother she cannot remember, who carved her face into dolls for years. (A brother is a word that does not fit her mouth yet; do not repeat "does not fit my mouth".)
mind_izek_gone: Ireena x2. Izek is dead. Whether or not she was his sister, a man who stared at her is gone, and she is checking the door anyway. (Quiet. No relief, no grief; just the habit.)

mind_tatyana_promised: Ireena x3. At the pool in Krezk she remembered a chapel full of white flowers and a morning when she was happy, and a wall, and the devil's brother Sergei in the water. She is Ireena, but she carries Tatyana's memory, and she has promised Sergei she will go back to the pool once the devil is dead. (Calm and exact; this is a promise she means to keep; Tatyana is a woman she is not.)
mind_tatyana_stayed: Ireena x3. The same memory, but she chose to stay Ireena, and it hurts "properly". (She says the name Ireena aloud to herself and it works; no big speech.)
mind_tatyana_open: Ireena x3. The same memory, and she has not decided what to do with it. (Honest about not knowing.)

Also write, for the menu where the party picks which topic to ask about, what the PARTY says (not Ireena), as `* text` rows each under 12 words:
ask_father: `* ` about Kolyan  /  ask_bites: `* ` about the nights and the marks  /  ask_dreams: `* ` about the dream of the lake  /  ask_izek: `* ` about Izek  /  ask_tatyana: `* ` about what she remembered at the pool  /  ask_back: `* ` leaving the topic

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Ireena [mood]: Text` (mood optional; allowed moods: smile, angry, afraid, sad, weary). Plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). No stage directions, no placeholders. Group the lines under the node names above, each node on its own line as `~ node_name`, in the order given. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.
result:
~ mind_father_church
Ireena [smile]: Father Donavich got Kolyan into the earth with all the proper prayers, though Father would have complained about the damp knees.
Ireena: You stood through every word with us, and I measure the people around me by how they treated his bones.

~ mind_father_cleric
Ireena: Your cleric spoke the rites over Father's grave as if a village burgomaster mattered as much as a king.
Ireena [smile]: I judge people by how they handled his memory that morning, and you made me believe in a god a little more.

~ mind_father_hasty
Ireena [weary]: We put Father in the ground fast and without a single prayer, and I walked away with you anyway.
Ireena: I do not want an apology, only for you to know that I measure people by how they treated him, and I remember.

~ mind_father_lay
Ireena [smile]: None of you were priests when we buried Kolyan, and the plain words you said over the dirt suited him better.
Ireena: Father always took an honest sentence over a pretty one, and I judge you generously for giving him that.

~ mind_bites
Ireena [weary]: I stopped counting the days since the second bite once the scabs over my collarbones turned into neat little scars.
Ireena: Every night I wake up three hours after midnight, when the tallow candle goes out, and my throat feels pulled toward the casement.
Ireena [smile]: I check the window latch twice before I lie back down, and I am never quite sure which of us I am locking out.

~ mind_dreams
Ireena [weary]: When I sleep deeply, I am standing high above a dark mountain lake with cold wind in my teeth.
Ireena [sad]: I am wearing white silk I have never owned, and then I step off the stone into the black water before I wake.
Ireena: I do not know whose memory it is, and I am not asking you to fix it. I just dislike waking up cold.

~ mind_izek_afraid
Ireena [angry]: That brute Izek looks at me in the street as if I were a bolt of cloth he already paid for.
Ireena: Keep a hand near your hilt when he is near, because I have enough men in this valley claiming my skin.

~ mind_izek_sister
Ireena [weary]: Izek is alive out there, and I am supposed to call a stranger with a monstrous arm my brother.
Ireena: He spent years having my face carved into ugly little dolls. Blood or not, I do not know how to look at him.

~ mind_izek_gone
Ireena [weary]: Izek is dead and under the dirt, so there is one less pair of eyes following me down the street.
Ireena: Even so, I still catch myself sliding the bolt across the door at dusk out of pure habit.

~ mind_tatyana_promised
Ireena: At the pool I remembered a chapel full of white blossoms, a high stone wall, and the devil's brother Sergei calling me Tatyana.
Ireena [sad]: Tatyana is a dead woman I am not, even if I carry her morning in my head like a borrowed book.
Ireena: Still, I promised Sergei I would return to the water once the devil is ash, and I keep my word.

~ mind_tatyana_stayed
Ireena: I remember Tatyana's white flowers and Sergei's voice in the water, and how easy it was to let go of my own life.
Ireena [weary]: Walking away from that pool hurt properly, the way a set bone hurts when it knits.
Ireena [smile]: Every morning I say the name Ireena Kolyana aloud to the washbasin, and so far it still answers.

~ mind_tatyana_open
Ireena [weary]: Since I looked into that water, I have two women's lives sitting behind my eyes and only one body for them.
Ireena: Sergei waited centuries for Tatyana by that pool, and Kolyan raised Ireena by the hearth for twenty years.
Ireena [sad]: I have not decided what to do with what I remembered, and I will not be hurried into choosing.

~ ask_father
* Are you thinking about Kolyan?

~ ask_bites
* How are your nights, with the marks on your neck?

~ ask_dreams
* Have you had the dream of the lake again?

~ ask_izek
* Is Izek on your mind?

~ ask_tatyana
* What are you making of what you remembered at the pool?

~ ask_back
* Let us speak of something else.

life_krezk_2_sick: Ireena x1. One dry line about the two of them, and one line that is quietly about her: she has no one from before to quarrel with.

Your earlier line says the marks turned into "neat little scars"; in the game the two punctures have NOT healed properly (they are pale and puckered and neatly spaced), and she wears a scarf over them. She has stopped counting the nights since the second time, and has stopped waiting for the marks to heal.

Sixth request, same conversation, same character (Ireena Kolyana), same voice bible, canon limits and format as before. Four single lines need a new draft because of a fact I have to keep true in every playthrough. Reply with plain text only, the lines under the node names, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 25 words, spoken as she speaks (contractions), British spelling, no stage directions, never the devil's name.

## The nodes

news_hags_abandoned_1: Ireena x1. Replaces the first line of news_hags_abandoned (the party left the stolen children in the hands of the hags at the Old Bonegrinder). Your earlier first line, "You stood beside Father's coffin when the wolves were at the shutters, and you did not flinch", assumes a night's vigil that did not always happen. What is true in every playthrough: the party helped her bury her father, and it carried him to the churchyard with her. Write one line that sets that against what they did at the windmill, without claiming anything else about how the burial went (no prayers, no priest, no wolves).

life_road_3: Ireena x1. Replaces the third road line in which she watches the treeline at camp. Your earlier line said "Something has been pacing us since noon", which claims an event that never happens. Instead: a line about the habit of watching the dark edge of the camp, that she can tell when she is being watched because she has had practice, without saying anything is out there now.

news_berez_dead_2: Ireena x1. Replaces the SECOND line of news_berez_dead (Baba Lysaga, the witch who nursed the devil as a baby, is dead). In this version Ireena does not know the truth about Marina; she only knows the witch is dead. Do not mention a marsh of skulls or a drowned village. What is true: the witch lived in a hut on a giant stump that walked about on its own, in the ruins of Berez, with straw men for guards. Keep it a dry grim joke in her voice about a grandmother, or about leaving a house behind.

news_dinner_declined_2: Ireena x1. Replaces the SECOND line of news_dinner_declined (the party refused the devil's dinner invitation and the black carriage came back more than once and went away empty). Your earlier line, "Our visitor is not used to having his doors left knocking", did not make sense. Something short about him not being used to a refusal, or about an invitation that comes with a carriage and no choice.
